articleTitle: Motor protection and control and systems
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: P&B, formed in 1932, have manufactured motor protection relays for almost 50 years. They continue to manufacture electromechanical relays whilst an increasing amount of their production is microprocessor-based. They, like several other protection manufacturers, are going through a quiet revolution as they move from protection only to protection and control disciplines. Here, they offer a view on the various protection alternatives together with their merits, reliability and overall capabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The B to N of electrical standardisation: the route from IEC 364 to national standards
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The approximation of standards and rules for electrical installations is proceeding steadily, if slowly, throughout the major countries of the world. It is proceeding rather more quickly in Europe, in particular in the Common Market. However while the words (in translation) may be similar, the results in the form of electrical installations may be or are markedly different as a result of national conditions and national practices. These differences do not produce installations which are dangerous, in spite of our belief that this is so, any more than a UK installation carried out in France and Germany would be dangerous in spite of the belief that the French and the Germans that this is so. Here, the author argues that the great hope for standardisation in Europe is that UK contractors will carry out French style installations in France and Germany style installations in Germany, and German and French contractors carry out UK style installations in accordance with the IEE Regulations, BS7671 in the United Kingdom.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The problems of access to continental markets for UK electrical contractors
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The author describes some of the problems that UK-based, small and medium-sized electrical contractors are likely to encounter when seeking to work in one of the continental Member States of the European Communities (EC). This perspective has been adopted in order to highlight the three key issues concerning the operation of the Single Market in connection with the activities of electrical contracting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cable installation: an overview of European & UK practice
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: There are marked differences between some European countries philosophies and practices for the application of power cables and UK practice. The author concentrates on low voltage multicore cables and addresses some of these differences from a user's point of view, highlighting areas to be considered when using cables in the UK which are constructed to other national standards. Installations in hazardous areas have not been considered in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lightning protection of electronic equipment-an arm's length view
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: Electronic equipment connected via cables leaving the relative safety of a building's equipotential zone, is vulnerable to damage from lightning transients. The purpose of this paper is to review the nature of the threat, how it may be satisfactorily dealt with, and provide some useful references. The importance of the method of installation and cabling is highlighted in terms of basic electrical theory, in the hope that an appreciation of the underlying principles will help the installer coping with practical problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The EMC directive-will it lead to compatible installations?
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The author aims to answer six questions about electromagnetic compatibility (EMC): (1) what is it?; (2) why are we interested?; (3) what are the legal requirements?; (4) how do we comply?; (5) what guidance is available?; and (6) what is the electrical contractors' association doing to help? Conclusions are drawn as to whether the EMC Directive will naturally lead to compatible installations or whether some additional guidance is required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operation and maintenance-the users view point
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The author argues that a client should understand that to achieve the most cost effective operation he must respect the services of the engineers he employs, whether they be designers, installers, operations or maintenance and each should listen to the views of the other. In order to fully appreciate the requirements for maintenance it is necessary to define the extent of the electrical installation and therefore he suggests that we define the areas as: (1) mains supply-33 kV, 11 kV, main LV switch board generator, UPS transformers; (2) distribution-LV networks and distribution boards; and (3) lighting and small power circuits-luminaries, portable appliances. While the application of maintenance to each area will vary, the underlying principles remain unchanged.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The selection & testing of cables & junction boxes for fire-alarm & safety systems
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: Although it could be a reasonably logical requirement, there is no existing single standard which covers the selection and testing under fire conditions, of the electrical apparatus which might be utilized in a fire alarm, emergency lighting or other similar system. Here, the author describes how the IEE regulations (BS7671) whilst recognizing the validity of BS476 as a test standard for intumescent protection pillows, seals etc., still does not, unfortunately, relate, as well as it might, with the fire standard BS5839 and, it may be argued, could provide better guidance if sections 526 and 527 were amplified to suggest BS476 as a system test standard for every component in a fire alarm or emergency lighting system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: HV/LV distribution network design for Waterloo International and Waterloo domestic station
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The new International Terminal will be a major landmark in London and it is important that a secure electrical power supply is incorporated. For this reason the power supply system of the Waterloo International was designed with two independent 11 kV high voltage supplies. The primary (nonessential) supply is derived from London Electricity plc (LE plc) and the traction (essential) supply derived from British Rail (BR) Electrification. The total maximum demand of Waterloo International is approximately 3.1 MVA on the LE plc primary HV supply network and 2.2 MVA on the BR traction HV supply network under essential conditions. The author describes how the LE plc supply is provided through three feeders to provide a 7 MVA total capacity supply. One feeder is connected direct to the zone substation and the other two are connected to the distribution network. The 7 MVA load can be maintained with the loss of any one feeder.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of the latest AI & IT tools to promote the most effective use of the IEE wiring regulations
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: Despite the success with the use of computers in the power industry, there remains a large class of problems that eludes solution using conventional software. These problems are usually solved by experts, require judgement, based on experience gained over a period of time and involve imprecise knowledge that cannot be formulated into an algorithm or a mathematical mode. The authors describe how the interpretation and application of the IEE wiring regulations is just such a problem concerning the application of a complex set of rules, procedures and standards, which, by reason of their format, are not easy to apply to specific problems. As such they provide an ideal example of an area of work where expert systems can assist in the engineering design of electrical installations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safety and legislation related to electrical installation engineering in Europe
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The author describes how members of the electrical installation world, have been both far-seeing and fortunate over the years. Not only have the safety issues associated with electricity been identified from the inception of the industry but appropriate codes of practice and standards for equipment and installations have also been established. These have been under continuous development since the start of this area of engineering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: Since January 1st 1993, the Common Market with its new face, the Unique Market, has come into force, at least on the level of principles. Here, in terms of electrical installation engineering in Europe, the author presents a general oversight of the possible problems, which may be classified under the following categories: (1) standards (wiring rules; equipment standards, mixing of different wiring, rules); (2) regulations (of several natures and aims); and (3) approval of contractors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Actions carried out by the French contractor's association 'SERCE' to improve safety on electrical installations
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: After a brief presentation of the SERCE organisation and duties, the author shows that the SERCE has been promoting, for a long time, a safety and accident prevention policy for its members. The results of these actions have been characterized by an improvement of statistical data but a still more powerful effort had to be made to the extend the accident prevention spirit in working places. In this regard a campaign on safety in work places was launched in September 1992 and its first conclusions are presented here.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Approaching fault-free electrical installation in building
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: Since the introduction of the IEE wiring regulations 15th Edition in year 1981, several major changes have occurred in Hong Kong affecting the designers, contractors and operating personnel of the electrical installation in buildings. The author outlines the relevant documents which set out fundamental requirements on the design, installation and maintenance aspects of the electrical installation and intend to achieve a common goal which is to avoid electrical hazard. The hazard includes the electric shock, injury and fire risk.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System earthing behaviour and its interaction with lightning protection system
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The five types of protective earthing systems for industrial and commercial power systems systems behave differently under the same earth fault conditions. Having dissimilar loop resistances and reactances in the systems, the fault currents significantly deviate in magnitudes and resonance behaviour. The 16th IEE wiring regulations recognizes this phenomenon and contributes solutions. The author supplements the discussion put forward by the regulations and related articles. The author also draws readers' attention to open-neutral faults and the interaction of lightning protection systems with the protection earthing systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Inspection, testing and verification (of electrical installations)
publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: Part 7 of the BSI 7671; 1992-Requirements for Electrical Installations (The IEE Wiring Regulations) covers inspection and testing and Chapter 71 contains the requirements for initial verification. Here, the author describes how initial verification requires that an installation be inspected and tested as the work proceeds, ie during erection and before being put into service, in order to verify that the design of the installation, the selection of materials and the equipment as well as the methods of installation, all conform to the relevant Regulations. Testing and inspection are also covered in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: The initial design concept of electrical supply to Barclays Data Centres relied upon two completely independent incoming mains, either of which would adequately support the center load. Diesel standby was installed to cater for outages affecting both incoming supplies. Some three years ago a review took place from which a successful business case was made to retrospectively install five large UPS systems into four centers. This paper sets out to outline:- research into equipment types, their characteristics and tests applied; selection of equipment; strategy for installation; design constraints and compromises; and conclusions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1993 International Conference on Electrical Installation Engineering in Europe
abstract: One of the most important parts of the design process for distribution systems is the selection of power cable sizes. There are many variables to be taken into account, therefore the result must be somewhat of a compromise. Where several criteria apply to a design process then it could be worth searching for the optimal combination, and this is the purpose of this paper. The distribution systems considered here are those of an LV system end-user, rather than a distributor, of energy. However, the conclusions are generally applicable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
